concerns.text: The proxy k_norm = |Δτ_hand| / (max(|Δv_object|, ε) * N) is presented as a friction proxy without sufficient justification that this ratio isolates friction; torque and velocity derivatives also depend on object geometry and mass, threatening construct validity.

The GLMM will be fit on data from only 10 novel objects. No power analysis is provided; with such a small number of random‑effect levels the model may be under‑powered to detect the policy effect, risking a Type II error.

Randomizing k_norm isolates the estimator but does not control for other object‑specific factors (e.g., mass, geometry) that also vary across trials, which could confound the attribution of performance gains to the estimator.

The percentile thresholds (90th/10th) for scaling rewards are chosen arbitrarily; without a sensitivity analysis or theoretical grounding, it is unclear whether these thresholds are appropriate for all objects.

The correlation experiment regresses k_norm against ground‑truth friction while k_norm also includes the normal force N, which varies with object mass and contact geometry. This may attenuate the observed Pearson r and jeopardize the claim that k_norm is a valid friction proxy.
